text: A model endpoint that handles ten requests a minute fine can fall over at ten thousand — scaling inference is about staying ahead of that, not reacting after it happens.

Azure Autoscale settings live on the resource's Scale out page — the same blade behind an App Service plan hosting a self-hosted inference API, reached through Configure, scoped to that specific resource.

From there it's a choice: manual scale holds a fixed instance count, while custom autoscale reacts to a schedule or to metrics — the setting that actually lets an inference service grow and shrink with real demand instead of guessing at a number up front.

A rule is where that reaction gets defined — threshold, duration, and action. This one decreases the instance count by one when average CPU stays under 20 percent for 10 minutes, so idle capacity doesn't sit there costing money.

A web app usually scales on CPU or request count. An AI inference endpoint's bottleneck is rarely the CPU at all — it's GPU utilization, queue depth, or token throughput — so the rule has to target whatever's actually saturated, not whatever's easiest to measure.
Scale on what's actually the bottleneck, not just what Autoscale measures by default. Next up: letting an AI app authenticate to these services without a password sitting in the code at all.
